    - heading "BOUNDARY TEST" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Non-empty
      - text: At least one point satisfies all inequalities. ✓
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Closed
      - text: Includes its boundary lines (≤ or ≥). ✓
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Finite
      - text: Does not extend infinitely in any direction. ✓
    - heading "POINT TEST for P(2, 3)" [level=2]
    - table:
      - rowgroup:

    - paragraph: P(2, 3) satisfies all → inside the feasible region.
    - article:
      - heading "WHAT IS A BOUNDED FEASIBLE REGION?" [level=2]
      - paragraph: A feasible region is bounded when all of its points fit inside a finite disk. It can be a polygon, a single point or a line segment.
    - article:
      - heading "COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: COMMON MISCONCEPTION
      - paragraph: Removing a constraint does not always make a region unbounded. Other constraints may still provide finite limits.

    - paragraph: Determine whether the system has a bounded feasible region, then list its corner points.
